items.definition: Submerged vegetation and seaweed gathered from the ria and used as fertilizer for sandy farmland; the moliceiro's traditional cargo.
Sail; one of the old methods of propelling the moliceiro.
Pole used by the crew to push the boat along, especially when there was no wind during work.
Towing the boat along the water from the bank by a line; an old propulsion method.
The moliceiro's load capacity: the amount of moliço it could carry.
Side of the hull; a long stretch amidships was lowered to ease loading heavy cargo aboard.
Waterline; the midship side edge sank below it once the load reached a certain amount, easing the loading manoeuvre.
Large drag rakes used to gather moliço and mud from the bottom, then hauled into the boat.
Bow; built markedly raised so poling crew work on a slope, gaining better efficiency with less effort than on a flat surface.
The working task or labour of gathering moliço, during which propulsion might have to be by pole.
Sloping surface on which poling crew work, giving better efficiency with less effort than a flat surface.
Stern; raised to support a very large rudder.
Rudder; very large, wide and shallow, allowing effective steering in the shallow moliço grounds.
Shallow waters of the moliço grounds, where the wide, shallow rudder was needed to steer effectively.
Shallow areas of the ria where moliço was harvested.
Caulking, sealing the hull's seams; aided by tarring the sides.
Black pitch coating the hull sides to help caulk and protect the pine wood from weather and water.
Pine wood, the material of the moliceiro hull.
Side of the hull, tarred black; its large surfaces were later decorated.
Port side of the boat, where a painted panel was first made, then repeated on the other side.
Starboard side of the boat, which received a painted panel matching the port side.
Stern deck area, whose black side surfaces were also decorated.
Painted decorative panels on the bow and stern, a folk art that developed from the boats' decoration.
Farming tools and implements, such as rakes, improved by farmers to harvest moliço.
